summary_original: Hello! I'm Yoni Skolnik, the set design lead for Reality Fracture , and I'm thrilled to get a chance to tell y'all about the process of designing the set's echoed pairs. Starting out, I was very nervous about the alternate-reality concept. Although the Time Spiral block is a personal favorite of mine, it's famously known for having alienated players who aren't deeply familiar with Magic . In exploratory design and vision design, we united around three pillars. Garruk remains far away. She pays them no attention. Her world is in her arms, and it is still warm from life. Vraska allows herself permission to mourn; grief wells up as an endless wave. Then, impossibly, she feels Liliana next to her. The necromancer kneels, laying her hands on his body. There is no magic. There is no malice. Vraska sees tears on her cheeks, watches the tremble in her lips. "It is so much more," Liliana says, too quietly for it to be a conversation. Vraska isn't certain what she means … until she remembers. She remembers what Jace shared of Liliana on that riverbed all those years ago. Will you be sad when I die?
